transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-12-30
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 45m
- Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE); Ethan Chen (Redwood SE); Priya Patel (Atlas Head of ML); Rajesh Kumar (Atlas Platform Eng); Emily Wong (Atlas Security); Liam O'Neil (Atlas Product)

Topics: rollout / go-live planning, canary strategy, A/B vs feature flag, monitoring & alerts, runbook, security signoff, pricing

---

00:00 Sofia: okay hello everyone thanks for joining, uh this is our weekly poc sync. today the focus is the rollout plan and runbook, we want to make sure the canary, the monitoring and the security checklist are all lined up

00:18 Priya: yep thanks Sofia, quick context 1 our goal is to cut over the payments assistant to Redwood inference for NLU scoring. we want a small canary first, then ramp to 100% over a week if metrics look good

00:35 Ethan: great, thanks. we propose a two-phase canary: phase 1 is 5% traffic for 48 hours, phase 2 25% for 72 hours, then 100% ramp if no regressions. do you have target s-lo's you want to hit?

00:50 Priya: latency 95p under 350ms end-to-end, and error rate under 0.5%. cost is factor but latency is primary. also we want to validate model quality using our eval set 1 to catch any regressions

01:05 Rajesh: technical note 1 current infra is k8s in our VPC, we will run Redwood Private in the VPC with our KMS. need details on networking ports and firewall rules

01:20 Ethan: we sent the network guide earlier, but i'll resend. also note Redwood Dedicated is an option if you want reserved capacity. dedicated pricing sheet will be with Sofia after the call

01:36 Emily: security gating 1 we need audit logs, SSO integration (SAML), and evidence for SOC2 controls. also want KMS/HSM integration tests and data residency proof

01:50 Sofia: understood. Emily, we'll share SOC2 artifact pack and an evidence plan. can you confirm the date you need signoff by?

02:02 Emily: ideally by Jan 12 so we can align with our release window the following week

02:12 Sofia: ok noted. on canary routing 1 Priya, do you want user-level segmentation (by org id) or percentage-based sampling?

02:24 Priya: percentage-based sampling is easier for now, but we'll keep org-based if we need to target specific tenants. initial 5% randomized sampling is fine

02:36 Ethan: for monitoring we'll push these metrics: p95 latency, p99 latency, token throughput, error rate (5xx/4xx), model quality delta on eval set, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll provide Grafana dashboards and Prometheus metrics endpoints.

02:54 Rajesh: also need KV cache warmup strategy. cold-starts spike latency for long contexts, so how do we pre-warm?

03:07 Ethan: good point 1 we recommend prefix caching for known flows and a small warmup job that primes KV cache for top 10 intents. we'll include runbook steps to run that job during low traffic windows

03:23 Liam: on A/B vs canary 1 product asks if we can do A/B test of two model variants (v1 quantized vs v2 full precision) to measure cost/latency/quality tradeoffs

03:36 Sofia: yes we support A/B. the rollout plan can run a 10% A/B where 5% goes to variant A and 5% to variant B within the overall 10% canary. need to agree on success metrics for quality and cost to pick winner

03:51 Priya: success metrics: QA score delta <1% on our eval, latency delta <50ms p95, and cost per 1k tokens within 10% of baseline

04:06 Ethan: noted. we'll surface quality regressions to the eval dashboard and set an alert if delta >1%

04:18 Sofia: about cutover windows 1 are you aiming for business hours or weekend?

04:24 Priya: business hours first, small canary. full cutover we'd like weekend window to reduce impact if rollback needed.

04:34 Sofia: ok. suggested plan: canary Jan 6-8 (5% -> 25% ramp as discussed), review metrics on Jan 9, and full cutover Jan 13 (weekend window Jan 13-14) if green.

04:50 Rajesh: that timeline works. need to put the runbook into our incident playbooks repo and include rollback steps (manual switch to old endpoint + traffic split rollback)

05:06 Ethan: runbook highlights we'll include: pre-cutover checklist, KV cache warmup job, health checks, rollback steps, smoke tests (sample queries), alert thresholds, and contact list. we'll link the runbook in the follow-up email

05:22 Emily: for security tests please add a step to validate request/response logs are scoped and that PII is redacted at the edge. also confirm retention period for logs

05:35 Ethan: default retention is 30 days for request logs, we can adjust per contract. we'll document log retention and provide a config option in the private deployment

05:48 Sofia: ok next, pricing 1 Priya you mentioned cost sensitivity. we can give a Dedicated commit sheet and also optimization recommendations (quantization, batching, cache) to reduce unit cost

06:02 Priya: yes please send the Dedicated pricing and the recommended quantization profiles for our workload. we might do a baseline run with full-precision and run a budgeted A/B to decide

06:15 Sofia: will do. i'll send a spreadsheet with projected monthly costs for 5k qps and 10k qps and include uplift for dedicated vs hosted

06:28 Liam: one more 1 observability handoff: who owns the dashboards after cutover?

06:34 Rajesh: platform will own infra alerts, product will own quality dashboards. need clear ownership in runbook; we will make oncall rotations in PagerDuty

06:45 Ethan: we'll add owners to each dashboard and a short doc for who to page for each alert

06:53 Sofia: great. recap and next steps 1 can we go around quickly? Priya?

07:00 Priya: confirm canary samples (5% then 25%), finalize A/B metrics, and review runbook. action: Priya to confirm traffic segmentation by Jan 4

07:12 Rajesh: I'll add firewall rules and do network test once we get the port list, action: Rajesh to complete firewall test by Jan 5

07:20 Emily: security tests and SOC2 evidence timeline, action: Emily to provide required evidence list by Jan 5

07:28 Ethan: publish runbook draft + dashboards by 2026-12-31, include warmup scripts

07:36 Sofia: send dedicated pricing + contract template + SOC2 artifact pack by 2026-12-31

07:44 Liam: i'll coordinate product acceptance criteria and be available during canary

07:50 Sofia: perfect, we'll send follow-up with links: runbook draft, Grafana dashboard, network guide, and pricing spreadsheet. any other questions?

07:58 Priya: none from me, thanks everyone

08:02 Sofia: thanks all, talk soon
